title: Split-Session Cluster GARCH Overnight/Intraday Tail Decomposition as IBS Entry Filter
source: arXiv:2607.03669 (Jul 2026) — "Split-Session Cluster GARCH for Overnight and Intraday Returns: The Role of Tail Heterogeneity" (Chen, Hansen, Tong)
description: The IBS mean-reversion strategy (H062-H112) profits from intraday reversal of within-session range extremes. Chen, Hansen & Tong (2026) show that overnight and intraday returns have structurally different tail behavior — convolution-t distributions with session-specific and sector-specific tail parameters. This creates a hypothesis: on days when the overnight return is large (tails of the overnight distribution), the intraday reversal may be muted or amplified depending on tail regime. H476 uses the overnight/intraday decomposition to construct a volatility-regime gate for IBS entries: when overnight realized variance is in the top decile (large overnight gap), skip the intraday IBS entry as market is likely in a fat-tail regime where direction uncertainty is high.
content_summary: Paper proposes Split-Session Cluster GARCH (SSC-GARCH): models multivariate daily returns as sum of overnight component + intraday component, each with a convolution-t distribution that allows tail parameters to differ across trading sessions and GICS sector clusters. Applied to US equities in 6-asset and 100-asset experiments, finds pronounced tail heterogeneity: overnight returns have systematically heavier tails than intraday returns (avg overnight tail index ~3.8 vs intraday ~5.2), and tail dependence clusters align with GICS sectors. For the H476 adaptation: (1) estimate session-specific realized variance RV_overnight and RV_intraday from daily OHLC data using O=open, C_prev=prior close, H/L/C; (2) when RV_overnight exceeds IS-calibrated 80th percentile, the overnight gap signal suggests a fat-tail day where intraday price action is less mean-reverting (more trend-following, as large overnight gaps often continue intraday); (3) suppress IBS long entry on XLK/SMH/IGV when overnight gap condition is active. Alternative Var B: replace suppression with size scaling (halve position on fat-tail overnight days). Var C: amplify IBS entry on SMALL overnight returns (thin tail = higher probability of intraday reversal).
variants: Var A: Skip IBS entry when overnight_rv > IS-80th-pct threshold (binary gate)
Var B: Scale IBS position by (1 - overnight_rv_rank) — continuous weighting
Var C: Enter only when overnight_rv < IS-20th-pct (concentration on thin-tail sessions, inversion of A)
Var D: H112 IBS baseline (unfiltered, sanity check)
gate: OOS Sharpe > 2.129 (H112 IBS baseline) AND MaxDD improvement vs -18%
data_requirements: yfinance daily OHLC for XLK, SMH, IGV. Overnight return = log(open_t / close_{t-1}). Intraday return = log(close_t / open_t). Realized variance proxy: squared overnight return. No additional data sources needed.
implementation_notes: Key implementation: overnight_rv = (log(open_t / close_{t-1}))**2. Rolling IS window to calibrate 80th pct threshold. Overnight_rv_rank = percentile of current overnight_rv in trailing 252-day window. IBS = (close - low) / (high - low) as before. Entry condition: IBS < 0.2 AND overnight_rv < threshold_80. Exit: close of same day (IBS strategy is daily). Transaction costs: same as H112 ($0.01/share assumed). CAUTION: 'overnight fat-tail' is a hypothesis — actual direction of effect on IBS win rate uncertain. May find that big overnight gaps are followed by stronger intraday continuation (trend day), not reversal. Var C tests the complementary hypothesis (small overnight = stable day = higher reversal quality). SSC-GARCH itself requires statsmodels or custom MLE — not needed for this proxy adaptation; we use realized variance as a direct observable proxy for the overnight tail regime.
